item: Wave 6 Q-02: public page bodies fit the window at 320, 390, 768 and 1280 with the text at 200 percent (home, how it works, corridors, network, trust)
spec: Conductor instruction of 6 Nov (Wave 6 Q-02, found by the header build); docs/revamp/specs/layout-budget.md
changed: tests/browser/public-large-text.spec.ts (new): sweeps home, how it works, corridors, network and trust at 320, 390, 768 and 1280 with the root text at 200 percent, measuring the whole page (header and footer included). It fails on a box past a window edge, in-flow text running out of its own box, or any sideways scroll. Decoration placed on top (absolutely positioned) and visually hidden text are not counted.

apps/web/app/globals.css, one block at the end: one-column grids may shrink their track (corridors, directions, progress, steps, intro list), the closing band wraps its button under its words above 700 px and its text breaks, tags may take a second line, long words in step cards and headings break, a button or link never grows past its column, and the intro list stacks its rows through a container query when it is narrower than twenty letters (a tablet at large text).

apps/web/components/home-landing.css: the home player's record tabs wrap, its caption puts the controls under the words, the six steps take a second row only when each no longer has room for its number, the field list goes to one column, the boarding passes give their stub less width on a narrow card, plan rows shrink their label column, and through container queries the shortlist and the quote table tighten and stack only when the player is narrower than a few words (large text on a phone).
apps/web/components/home-mission-player.tsx: each quote cell carries data-column so a stacked cell can name its supplier in front of its value; nothing is added when the table is side by side.

apps/web/components/site-footer.css: the footer promise and every footer link break long words; the footer's two actions and the phone link columns (two columns of links) go to one column through a container query only when the block is narrower than a dozen letters of its own text, so nothing changes at normal text size.

tests/browser/public-normal-text.spec.ts (new): 100 percent guards. The home player's step marks, field columns, tab row, plan label column, pass stub, quote columns and buyer columns at every one of the six screens and six widths (320 to 1440) are asserted against a table produced by the same probe on a main build (1c0f75e) and equal on this branch (36 of 36 rows); the footer link columns, the closing band on one row beside its button at 1024 to 1440, the /network band at 768 (text column wider than 300 px; on main 80 px) and the six step marks in one row at every 32 px from 320 to 1920 (at 1024 the player is about 483 px wide and the marks need about 472).
preserved: Every element, word, link, id and test hook. No server, database, request or payload change. English only.

At normal (100 percent) text size, measured by comparing every element's position and size on main and on this branch for the five pages at 320, 390, 768 and 1280, these are the only differences: (1) the closing band's text box is wider at 1024, 1280 and 1440 with the same wrapping and the button where it was (guarded by 'the closing band keeps its words and its button side by side'); (2) /network at 768: main squeezes the band's text column to 80 px, and the band now wraps its button under the words, so it is a defect fix, not a design change; (3) the footer, tags and public-page buttons can wrap or break where they used to overflow or clip, which only shows when they did not fit. Two normal-size regressions found in review were fixed and are guarded: the phone's two-column phase step ('the phone keeps its two-column phase step') and the home player's request fields staying two columns wide at every width ('the player fields stay two columns wide'), plus the caption keeping its controls beside its words at 320 ('the player caption keeps its controls beside its words').

The container queries count rem at the page's text size, so they do not apply at 100 percent on a phone; each shrink rule only takes effect once the content no longer fits. The tag wrapping is scoped to public pages (.ux-public), so signed-in pages keep the trust tag on one line.

100 percent comparison against main 1c0f75e, throwaway script not committed: every element's box on /, /how-it-works, /corridors, /network, /trust, /about and /privacy at 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440, and the home player at all six screens at each width, both from production builds. The full box comparison was run on a local build of my own version of the review fixes (a different commit from this head, same Q-02 styles), not on this exact head; on this head the same facts are asserted by the committed guards, which pass in the e2e run above. Differences from main are only those under normalSizeChanges.
openRisks: The sweep is a first guard, not a proof. Known gaps (follow-up): it exempts overflow:hidden containers and their clipped children, skips inline elements narrower than two pixels, has no pseudo-element or overlap check, no vertical clipping check, never measures a hidden phase panel or a closed details, uses a root font of 200 percent instead of 200 percent zoom (a 640 px window at 100 percent is not run), and does not cover about, institutions, privacy, sign-in, corridor details or /plan.

The overflow-wrap and wrap rules in normalSizeChanges item 3 have no per-rule 100 percent test; they are covered only by the element-box comparison above (uncommitted) and the home-player table. A long unbroken word in a public page at 100 percent would now break instead of overflow, which is the intended effect.

The step marks use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(4.5rem, 1fr)); at 1024 the margin is about 11 px (483 against 472). The new step-marks guard fails if a later change to the player's padding or the root font narrows it.
normalSizeChanges: Closing band (home, how it works, corridors, network, trust) at 1024, 1280 and 1440: the text block's box is wider (home at 1024: 461 to 582 px; at 1440: 461 to 950 px). The words wrap the same way, the button and the band height did not move. Guarded: public-normal-text 'closing band' and public-large-text 'closing band keeps its words and its button side by side'.

/network closing band at 768: main squeezes the text column to 80 px (band 520 px tall); now the words take 560 px and the button sits below (band 275 px tall). A defect fix. Guarded: public-normal-text '/network at 768'.

Wrapping and breaking rules (footer promise and links, tags, step cards, buttons, the home player's plan rows and passes): they act only when a word or box did not fit, so a page at 100 percent measured identical; unguarded as a class, because a rule that changes nothing has nothing to assert. Listed under openRisks.
